gloss: to come and go; to go back and forth

definitions.gloss: to come and go; to go back and forth; to travel between
definitions.explanation: To move repeatedly between two places, or to have regular interaction with someone involving visits in both directions.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}が{行|い}き{来|き}している。
{東京|とうきょう}と{大阪|おおさか}の{間|あいだ}を{行|い}き{来|き}する{生活|せいかつ}をしている。
examples.english: I live going back and forth between Tokyo and Osaka.

examples.japanese: {国境|こっきょう}を{自由|じゆう}に{行|い}き{来|き}できるようになったのは、つい{最近|さいきん}のことだ。
examples.english: It was only recently that people became able to freely travel back and forth across the border.

notes:
Describes repeated movement between two points, whether physical travel or regular contact between people. The noun form {行|い}き{来|き} is also common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}の{行|い}き{来|き}: people coming and going; foot traffic
- {行|い}き{来|き}が{多|おお}い: lots of traffic; busy
- {行|い}き{来|き}が{激|はげ}しい: heavy traffic
- {自由|じゆう}に{行|い}き{来|き}する: to come and go freely

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {往復|おうふく}する: to make a round trip — emphasizes a single there-and-back journey rather than repeated movement
- {通|かよ}う: to commute, go regularly — implies a habitual one-directional trip (e.g., to work or school)
- {出入|でい}りする: to go in and out — focuses on entering and leaving a specific place

USAGE:
Can describe both physical movement ({車|くるま}が{行|い}き{来|き}する) and social interaction ({手紙|てがみ}の{行|い}き{来|き} meaning 'exchange of letters').
